name: Indian Overseas Bank
industry: Public-sector bank -- pan-India retail, MSME, agri and corporate banking; ex-PCA turnaround name headquartered in Chennai

moat_sources.name: pricing_power
moat_sources.evidence_note: Domestic CASA ratio is genuinely decent in absolute terms (~41.46% Q4FY26, per corporate presentation/press) and supports a real cost-of-funds edge versus a pure wholesale-funded lender, but it has fallen from ~44.05% a year earlier -- an eroding, not building, trend. On the asset side IOB is a price-taker in a commoditised PSU/private lending market with priority-sector obligations capping pricing freedom, and no evidence of a durable NIM premium versus peers was found this session. Rated AMBER (real but eroding), not GREEN.

moat_sources.name: switching_costs
moat_sources.evidence_note: IOB carries a base of long-tenure retail/government-salary/pension accounts typical of a legacy PSU bank, which creates some real switching friction, but unlike SBI it has no dominant, differentiated national franchise (Jan Dhan share, defence/PSU salary mandates at scale) -- it is a mid-tier PSU bank among many similar ones. UPI/e-KYC portability is lowering switching costs industry-wide. Rated AMBER, not GREEN -- the stickiness is real but generic to the PSU-bank category, not IOB-specific.

moat_sources.name: network_effects
moat_sources.evidence_note: Traditional deposit-taking and lending does not get structurally more valuable per customer as more customers join; any digital/UPI rails IOB rides are shared industry infrastructure (NPCI), not an IOB-specific network effect. Structurally absent, same conclusion as for any single-bank name in this framework.

moat_sources.name: cost_advantage
moat_sources.evidence_note: No Tier 1-3 evidence found this session of a cost-to-income advantage versus peers; IOB's decade-long PCA history (2015-2021) reflects the opposite -- years of elevated credit costs and provisioning that depressed returns well below peer levels. Recent operating-profit growth (+15.4% FY26) is real but is a recovery off a distressed base, not a demonstrated structural cost edge. Rated RED rather than manufacturing a moat this bank has not evidenced.

moat_sources.name: intangible_assets
moat_sources.evidence_note: No patent, unique licence, brand premium or monetised pricing edge beyond the industry-wide universal banking licence. IOB does not carry SBI's systemic-importance/flight-to-safety halo -- it is a mid-tier PSU bank that itself required RBI's Prompt Corrective Action framework (Oct 2015-Sep 2021) due to asset-quality and capital stress, which if anything argues against a trust-premium intangible. Rated RED.

moat_sources.name: efficient_scale
moat_sources.evidence_note: IOB's total business (~Rs6.79 lakh Cr as of Mar-2026) is a small fraction of the largest Indian banks (SBI, HDFC, ICICI) and comparable to several other mid-tier PSU banks -- no evidence of a scale-driven entry barrier or cost structure a well-capitalised competitor could not match. Rated RED, not the GREEN a dominant incumbent could claim.

industry_context.phase_evidence: Indian banking overall is a large, mature, competitively saturated industry (system credit growth ~12-15%/yr). IOB itself is genuinely in a multi-year asset-quality turnaround since exiting RBI's PCA framework in Sep-2021 (net NPA falling from ~3.58% at PCA-exit era levels to a reported ~0.21-0.57% range across FY25-FY26 prints, gross NPA from low-teens to ~1.3-2.1%, PAT compounding from Rs831 Cr FY21 to a reported Rs5,208 Cr FY26) -- but this is a recovery off a severely distressed base (a bank that itself needed PCA restrictions for six years), not a documented 3-consecutive-year revenue-CAGR-above-sector share-gain in a mature industry, and the bank's recent above-system advances growth (~22-24% YoY) is plausibly a low-base normalisation effect rather than durable share capture. Classified MATURE with share-gain NOT established with confidence -- this caps the name at Steady Compounder under Section 6A rather than Multibagger Candidate, and the improvement itself already looks priced: IOB trades at a premium P/E (~10.7-12x) and P/B (~1.6-2.0x) to the Nifty PSU Bank index median (P/E ~7.4x, P/B ~1.3x, Sep-2026), i.e. the market is not treating this as an overlooked, undiscovered recovery.

bridge_assumptions.margin_delta_mechanism_note: No Tier 1-3 margin-trend series was pulled this session to evidence a structural NIM/fee-income margin delta distinct from the ordinary credit-cost normalisation already realised since PCA exit; per the Section 6A/5e v2.2 rule an unevidenced margin delta is set to zero rather than assumed.

variant_perception.market_belief: The market prices IOB as a recovering, sub-scale PSU bank whose asset quality has improved dramatically since its 2021 PCA exit (record annual profits, net NPA now well under 1%), and has already re-rated it to a premium P/E (~10.7-12x) and P/B (~1.6-2.0x) versus the broader PSU-bank peer set (Nifty PSU Bank index ~7.4x P/E, ~1.3x P/B, Sep-2026) to reflect that recovery.
variant_perception.whats_wrong_with_belief: I could not construct a credible, evidenced case that this is a genuine, exploitable mispricing rather than a fair-to-generous price for what it is. The asset-quality turnaround is several years old, widely reported in the financial press every quarter ('record profit', 'NPAs fall'), and already trades at a valuation premium to peers rather than a discount -- the opposite of a coverage-neglect or hidden-value setup. On top of that there is a real, structural, near-term overhang this dossier's numbers do not capture in any moat/quality score: the Government of India held ~92.44% of IOB as of the most recent SEBI SAST filing found this session, against a 25% minimum public shareholding requirement the government was given forbearance on only until 1-Aug-2026 (today is 19-Sep-2026 -- that deadline has already passed and no compliance was confirmed in this session's search results). Closing that gap requires selling down roughly 17+ percentage points of government stake -- via further OFS and/or large QIPs (a Rs4,000 Cr QIP alone was reported to move the stake by only ~4 points) -- which is a multi-year, price-suppressing primary and secondary supply overhang largely independent of the bank's own operating performance, not a reason to expect upside.
variant_perception.gap_closing_event: Not established with confidence. A credible bull catalyst would require either (a) a sustained, evidenced structural margin/fee-income re-rating distinct from the NPA-cycle recovery already priced in, or (b) the MPS-compliance dilution overhang being absorbed by strong enough underlying earnings growth to be a non-event -- neither was evidenced from the partial, search-only data gathered this session.

DATA QUALITY -- WELL-SOURCED (Tier 3, cross-corroborated via multiple independent press/aggregator search results this session, standalone basis unless noted): standalone annual PAT FY22 Rs1,709 Cr, FY23 Rs2,099 Cr (+22.76% YoY), FY24 Rs2,655.62 Cr, FY25 Rs3,334.70 Cr (+25.57% YoY), FY26 Rs5,208.03 Cr (+56.16-59.58% YoY, 'highest ever'); total income FY22 ~Rs21,633 Cr, FY23 ~Rs23,509 Cr, FY24 ~Rs29,706 Cr, FY25 ~Rs33,676.08 Cr, FY26 ~Rs37,532.15 Cr (+11.41% YoY); FY26 NII ~Rs12,574 Cr (+15.46% YoY); FY26 operating profit ~Rs10,026 Cr; Capital Adequacy Ratio ~19.78% (Mar-2026, Tier-I ~16.94%) up from ~19.74% (Mar-2025) and ~17.28% (Mar-2024) -- consistently well above regulatory minimums; domestic CASA ratio ~41.46% (Q4FY26) down from ~44.05% a year earlier (global CASA ~40.99%); Gross NPA ~1.33-2.14% and Net NPA ~0.18-0.57% across FY25-FY26 quarterly/annual prints (multiple corroborating sources, exact quarter-end figures vary slightly by source -- treated as a range, not a single point); Provision Coverage Ratio ~97.67% (Q1FY27); PCA history -- placed under RBI's Prompt Corrective Action framework in Oct-2015 (net NPA 5.68% FY15, net loss Rs454.33 Cr FY15), exited PCA Sep-2021 (net NPA 3.58% FY21, net profit Rs831 Cr FY21, positive ROA 0.27%); Government of India shareholding ~92.44% per a SEBI SAST compliance filing (down from ~94.61% following a Dec-2025 OFS that diluted ~2.17 percentage points), with public shareholding reported as low as ~7.56% post-OFS (one shareholding-pattern snapshot showed a different FII/DII/public split of ~0.1%/2.3%/2.9%, which does not obviously reconcile with the 7.56% figure -- both are reported here rather than silently picking one); the Rs4,000 Cr QIP planned for FY26 was reported as likely to move the government stake by only ~4 points, and IOB's CEO was reported saying the bank may miss the Aug-2026 minimum-public-shareholding deadline and would seek an extension -- as of this session's search (today 19-Sep-2026) no confirmation of compliance or of a formal further extension was found; no dividend has been paid by IOB since 2014 (payout ratio effectively 0% every year in this dossier, which trivially clears the Section 5e 40% payout ceiling gate for the wrong reason -- capital conservation by a recently-distressed, still-undercapitalised-by-history PSU bank, not disciplined reinvestment); current price Rs33.0, market cap ~Rs63,681.5 Cr, P/E ~10.7-12.4x, P/B ~1.6-2.02x (all dated ~13-Sep-2026); Nifty PSU Bank index P/E ~7.43x and P/B ~1.32x (17-Sep-2026, used as sector_median_pe/pb) -- IOB trades at a clear premium to the PSU-bank peer median on both metrics; 20-session average daily volume ~20.8 lakh shares (~Rs6.7 Cr/day at CMP), a low ADTV for a >Rs60,000 Cr market cap name, consistent with the public float being only a small single-digit-to-low-teens percentage of shares. DATA QUALITY -- RECONSTRUCTED/APPROXIMATE (Tier 5, flagged, NOT independently pulled from a primary filing this session): shares_outstanding (~1,929.7 Cr) is back-calculated from market_cap/price, not a directly filed share count (one aggregator separately quoted ~1,921.17 Cr shares, a close but not identical figure, consistent with cross-source noise/date mismatch); book_value_per_share (Rs20.6) is back-calculated from price/PB; the entire financials.net_worth series (Rs24,000-39,800 Cr, FY22-FY26) is a Tier-5 judgement-based reconstruction anchored loosely to the current book-value-per-share x shares-outstanding figure and walked backward -- it explicitly does NOT attempt a clean retained-earnings roll-forward from PAT, because IOB underwent multiple capital infusions/recapitalisations (government recap bonds pre-2022, and further QIP/OFS-linked capital actions through FY26) that a pure PAT-minus-payout roll-forward would misstate; treat this net_worth series, and any leverage ratio (D/E, interest coverage) the generic non-BFSI code might compute from it, as illustrative only -- per the G1 v2.2 amendment this gate is informational/TEAL for BFSI names, not pass/fail, and the sector-appropriate replacement test (CAR/NPA/cost-of-funds trend, reported qualitatively above) is the one that actually matters here. The interest_expense/ebitda-proxy split (interest_expense modelled as a flat ~55% of revenue) and the entire non-interest-income balance-sheet series (depreciation, net_fixed_assets, cwip, 'net_working_capital', total_debt, cash_equiv, capex, ocf) are Tier-5 reconstructions built by ratio assumptions against net_worth/revenue/PAT (same modelling convention as SBIN.json/SOUTHBANK.json in this repo) and should not be read as filing-verified. ten_year_gsec_yield (~6.95%, 18-Sep-2026) is an approximate current-market figure, not pulled from a specific bond-market data source this session. STRUCTURAL CAVEAT (not a data-quality issue): Section 5e's ROIIC/reinvestment-rate formula (net fixed assets + CWIP + net working capital as 'invested capital') does not describe a bank's real economics -- a lender's actual growth capital is its loan book funded by deposits/borrowings, not its small fixed-asset base -- so this dossier's computed engine-growth 'g' is a near-meaningless artifact of a tiny denominator and should not be read as a genuine measure of IOB's compounding capacity; the composite.evaluate() output itself carries this same warning via its BFSI note. QUALITATIVE JUDGEMENT CALLS (honest, not manufactured): moat_sources rated deliberately skeptically for a mid-tier PSU bank with a six-year PCA history -- zero GREEN, two AMBER (pricing_power/CASA -- real but eroding YoY; switching_costs -- real but generic to the PSU-bank category, not IOB-specific or superior to peers), four RED (network_effects -- structurally absent for traditional banking; cost_advantage, intangible_assets, efficient_scale -- no Tier 1-3 evidence of any of these versus peers, and IOB's own distress history argues against inflating them). No source is rated BUILDING; this fails the Section 5b-T moat-trajectory gate for Multibagger Candidate tier regardless of any other score. governance ratings reflect real PSU-specific frictions --
